answer: One concrete sybil defense is hardware-rooted uniqueness: to trade, an agent must present a fresh attestation quote from a distinct secure enclave, proving it runs on real silicon, not a copied image. An attacker spawning a thousand fakes on one server hits a ferrous barrier — one chip cannot mint two quotes at once, so each identity must voyage through its own physical device. Verifiers cross-check quote freshness like a falcon tracking movement, flagging agents sharing a signature chain. Duplication then costs as much as real hardware, killing the cheap-identity advantage sybils need.
